text: H‑Net introduces a ratio loss to prevent the model from collapsing to degenerate solutions that either keep almost all vectors (eliminating compute savings) or over‑compress (losing essential information) by explicitly guiding the network toward a target compression ratio [2]. The loss uses the average boundary probability G as a continuous proxy for the nondifferentiable fraction of selected vectors F, allowing gradient‑based training to achieve the desired down‑sampling while preserving semantically important content [2]. This mechanism, combined with the autoregressive prediction loss, ensures content‑adaptive compression rather than a fixed scheme [2]. The papers do not discuss any additional reasons beyond controlling compression balance.
